clue.text: He, a stoic, a smashing prime minister

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stoical man is praised as a terrific head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise but signals an anagram of HE A STOIC A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the title of the Irish head of government, equivalent to a prime minister.

clue.text: Keep out of Soweto, we reckon

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, concealed across them

explanation.surface: Someone guesses something should be kept out of a South African township.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: the strongest part of a castle. The letters sit across SoweTO WE Reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the central fortified building of a castle, a kind of stronghold structure.

clue.text: Leaders of our Liberal Democrats, advanced in years

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, so take the first letter of each

explanation.surface: Our Liberal Democrat leaders are getting on in age.
explanation.definitionFit: Being advanced in years means having lived a long time, i.e. being elderly.

clue.text: Show violence towards powerful member

definitions.meaning: to bully or coerce someone by physical force
a mighty limb, a member being an arm or leg

explanation.surface: Someone with a powerful limb turns violent.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce by force is the verb sense; read literally the words describe a muscular limb.

clue.text: Calm, primate eating nutritious seeds

indicators.note: one piece eats the other, taking it inside itself

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are nutritious seeds from pods

explanation.surface: A calm ape munches on healthy seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm here is a verb: to pacify or soothe someone who is angry.

clue.text: Label under meat dish reveals symbol

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: hash is a dish of chopped meat
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A label beneath a meat dish shows a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The # sign used on social media to mark topics is a symbol.

clue.text: Somebody touring clubs in the past

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second as a tourist goes round a place

parts.note: one means a person, somebody
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone used to go round golf or night clubs in former days.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Prophet using common sense about crazy paintings surrealist initially put up

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, i.e. around, the rest

parts.note: nous is British slang for common sense

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
art means paintings collectively

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A seer uses sense about wild surrealist paintings being hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' suggests hanging pictures, but in a down entry it reads the pieces upwards, giving STRADAM; 'about' wraps the sense word around that.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the sixteenth-century French seer famous for his prophecies.

clue.text: Holly, for example, enduringly popular

definitions.meaning: holly is a plant that keeps its leaves all year
a song or show that never goes out of fashion

explanation.surface: Someone named Holly has lasting appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly is a classic year-round leafy shrub; the same word describes a perennially popular hit.

clue.text: Accordingly, American follows half of them

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first, coming after it
half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: An American trails after half of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and accordingly both mean consequently or therefore.

clue.text: Action to secure both sides of dragline crane, maybe

indicators.note: one piece secures, holding inside it, the other

parts.note: action in the military sense is war or fighting

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A crane operator needs action to fix a dragline at each end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crane' looks like machinery, which suits dragline, but it is the long-legged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A crane is a long-legged bird that feeds in shallow water, an example of the category.

clue.text: Busy teashops needing to save time straightaway

indicators.note: the jumbled letters save, keeping inside them, the extra letter
busy suggests bustle and disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Crowded tea rooms must save time immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' signals an anagram of TEASHOPS, POSHASTE, and 'to save' places T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, immediately.

clue.text: Unnecessary to sound off about day with nothing on in retreat

indicators.note: the outer piece goes about, around, the inner one

parts.note: to rant is to sound off loudly

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: with nothing on means nude

explanation.surface: No need to complain about a day of naked retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns the naked day round to EDUND; 'about' has the complaining word go round it, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means superfluous, no longer needed.

clue.text: One not spotted in game

parts.note: a domino tile with no spots on either half, unnoticed only in the sense of having no pips

explanation.surface: A player went unnoticed during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as noticed, but it means marked with spots: dominoes tiles carry pips.
explanation.definitionFit: In dominoes, the tile with zero pips on both halves has no spots at all.

clue.text: Show lack of interest in Irish rugby

indicators.note: the letters are found in the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone is indifferent to Irish rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders briefly is the gesture of indifference.

clue.text: About to cross where French boy gets a Swiss roll, say

indicators.note: the outer piece crosses, spanning over, the inner ones

parts.note: re means about, concerning
ou is French for where
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A French lad crosses somewhere and is given a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled-up dish, of which a Swiss roll sponge cake is an example.

clue.text: Hot stuff, colour sergeant with band

parts.note: red is a colour
Sgt Pepper led the Lonely Hearts Club Band of the Beatles album

explanation.surface: A colour sergeant and his band make a sizzling act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colour sergeant' is a real army rank, but it splits: colour is RED, and the sergeant with a band is the Beatles' Sgt Pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum of this sort is spicy produce, food that is hot.

clue.text: Cook using good sieve

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, used for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A chef strains things through a decent sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook on a flat iron plate over heat is to prepare food that way.

clue.text: Publican's secret stock inside

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: inner means private, secret, as in inner thoughts
to keep goods is to stock them

explanation.surface: A landlord's private supply is kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Publican' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, keeping an establishment that serves drinks.

clue.text: Quandary of Miss Woodhouse perhaps, after returning hat

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: Jane Austen's heroine is in a fix after returning a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice, a predicament.

clue.text: Employed by London-based newspaper now and again

parts.note: working at a firm means employed by it
The Times is a London newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist works on The Times now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: At times means occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Put up piece for executioner

parts.note: to hang a picture is to put it up
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Someone puts up an artwork for an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman carries out death sentences by the gallows.

clue.text: Advance warning from principal teachers at university

parts.note: heads are head teachers, the principals of schools
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Headteachers at college give early notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A heads-up is a timely alert about something coming.

clue.text: The Spanish show respect in joint

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to bow is to show respect

explanation.surface: Spaniards show respect by bending a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Pay wife to decline

parts.note: to age is to grow older, to decline

explanation.surface: Someone pays their wife to say no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' suggests refusing, but here it means deteriorate with years.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the pay earned for work.

clue.text: Dramatist newspaper chief crossed

parts.note: Ben Travers was an English playwright known for farces
ed is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A playwright and a newspaper boss fell out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed' suggests angry, but it means went across.
explanation.definitionFit: Traversed means travelled across, went from one side to the other.

clue.text: Live adequately under daughter's roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under another comes after it
in a down clue the roof of a word is its top, so first letter

parts.note: well means satisfactorily, adequately

explanation.surface: Someone lives comfortably enough under their daughter's roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside, make one's home there.

clue.text: Line among pages may, unfortunately, mess around with one's feelings

indicators.note: the piece goes among, inside, the other letters
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A line among some pages may sadly toy with someone's emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb but is fodder: 'unfortunately' scrambles it with the pages, and 'among' drops the line's letter into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To play games with someone is to manipulate or toy with them emotionally.

clue.text: Chaplain might offer tramp religious education

parts.note: to pad is to tramp along on foot
RE is the school subject religious education

explanation.surface: A chaplain offers a vagrant some religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a vagrant noun but is the verb, walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a military chaplain.

clue.text: Pair, uneasy at first, entering function

indicators.note: one letter enters, going inside, the other piece

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: at first means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A couple feel uneasy when first arriving at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a twosome, two people together.

clue.text: Playboy's name missing from column, last in article

indicators.note: the abbreviation is missing, removed, from the word

parts.note: a rank is a line or column of soldiers

indicators.note: last in means take the final letter

explanation.surface: A magazine's name is missing from a column at the end of an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playboy' looks like the magazine but means a womaniser; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man about town, a libertine.

clue.text: Hooter goes at end of great championship game

indicators.note: the second piece goes at the end of the first

parts.note: superb means great, excellent
an owl is a hooter, from its call

explanation.surface: A horn sounds at the end of a great title match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a horn or nose but is the owl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the annual NFL championship game in American football.
